$comment: TEMPLATE ONLY — never loaded. Copy to $DRYDOCK_CONFIG_DIR/repo-registry.json (default ~/.drydock/configs/repo-registry.json) or point DRYDOCK_REGISTRY_PATH at your own file, then edit. This is DEPLOYMENT STATE: which repositories this factory may act on and what each one is allowed to do. It deliberately does not live in the source tree — the supervisor reads it live, so a file inside the tree would make policy changeable by switching branches, and drydock's own pathAllowlist covers `factory/`, meaning a self-run could edit the policy that governs it (see factory/repo-registry.ts registryPath() and research/multi-repo-factory-plan.md §5.28). Fields per repo: eligibilityLabel (the label that starts a run), autoMerge (false = runs stop at the draft PR), enabled, webhookId (this deployment's hook id — without it, failed deliveries for that repo are never swept), pathAllowlist (null = any non-protected path; vendor/ is protected everywhere regardless), protectedPaths, requireVerification (default true), oracleBoot (argv executed by behavior gates — shell metacharacters rejected at load), refine/refineLabel/prFeedback. Per-repo RUNTIME config (model pin, testCommand, setupCommand, budgets) is a separate file: <owner>_<repo>.json in the same directory.

repos.note: A repo the factory may auto-merge: it is a throwaway fixture with no history worth protecting.

autoMerge false and a narrow scope: runs stop at a draft PR for a human, and the oracles that judge a run sit outside the run's reach. Add a protectedPaths entry for anything a run must not amend — including its own test oracle once one exists.
